## Transportation  

### Data sources  

The transportation module is constructed based on a set of standard forecasts for inputs such as passenger miles traveled, vehicle miles traveled, existing vehicle stock, new vehicle sales, average vehicle occupancy, fuel efficiency, and population. These parameters are utilized to predict the vehicle miles traveled and resultant emissions. The scenario planning tool then utilizes selected intervention elasticities and proportional effects to calculate the potential reduction in emissions.

```{r tab-source-mode-var}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
source_mode_var <- ghg.sp::transportation_index$data_sources %>%
  left_join(transportation_index$modes, by = c("mode" = "mode_abbrev")) %>%
  left_join(transportation_index$variables, by = c("var" = "var_name")) %>%
  select(
    Mode = mode_description_1,
    Measure = var_description,
    Source = source_short
  ) %>%
  unique()


gt::gt(
  id = "tab-source-mode-var",
  data = source_mode_var,
  groupname_col = "Mode",
  caption = "Transportation variables and data sources"
) %>%
  gt::opt_row_striping(TRUE) %>%
  gt::tab_options(row_group.font.weight = "bold")
```

#### Source summaries

##### Market Acceptance of Advanced Automotive Technologies (MA3T) {#ma3t-doc}  

Model developed by Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) to simulate the diverse purchasing behaviors among individuals in the market place. You can read more about the model and find full documentation on the [ORNL website `r fontawesome::fa("external-link-alt")`](https://teem.ornl.gov/ma3t.shtml){target="_blank"}

```{r ma3t-graphic, out.width = "70%", fig.cap="MA3T model abstraction [@linMA3TModel2013]"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://www.ornl.gov/sites/default/files/ma3t1.png")
```

#### Metropolitan Council sources

##### Travel Behavior Inventory (TBI) {#metc-tbi}  

The Travel Behavior Inventory (TBI) is a 10-year program by the Metropolitan Council. It includes a household travel survey, a survey of on-board transit riders, and other travel behavior data collection.  

Key findings from the 2019 TBI can be found on the [Met Council website `r fontawesome::fa("external-link-alt")`](https://metrocouncil.org/Transportation/Performance/Travel-Behavior-Inventory/2019.aspx){target="_blank"}


##### Travel Demand Model {#metc-travel-demand}  

The Met Council, like all large metropolitan planning organizations, maintains a regional transportation forecasting model. The model is used to forecast travel for all types of transportation and highway and transit facility usage.  

The current regional travel demand forecast model is called an “activity-based model”, which means that it simulates transportation decisions made by individuals ranging from long-term (e.g. regular work/school location, whether to own an automobile), day-level (e.g, what activities to engage in, with whom, where, and when), and trip-level (what transportation mode to use, what route to take) in order to evaluate policy and investment choices  at a high level of detail.  

Other, more single-purpose forecast models are maintained by the Council as well, including a regional implementation of the FTA’s STOPS model for transitway ridership forecasting, as well as a regional park-and ride model.    

You can find more information on the [Met Council website `r fontawesome::fa("external-link-alt")`](https://metrocouncil.org/Transportation/Performance/Travel-Forecasting.aspx){target="_blank"}

###### Annual Energy Outlook values  {#aeo-values}  

The Annual Energy Outlook (AEO) is a report series by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) exploring long-term energy trends in the United States [@eiaAnnualEnergyOutlook2021]. 

You can read more on the [EIA website `r fontawesome::fa("external-link-alt")` ](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/aeo){target="_blank"}.  

```{r tab-aeo-values}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
ghg.sp::factor_values$aeo %>%
  mutate(
    aeo_scen = as.factor(aeo_scen),
    mode = as.factor(mode),
    metric = as.factor(metric),
    year = as.factor(year)
  ) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top",
    colnames = c(
      "AEO Scenario",
      "Mode",
      "Metric",
      "Year",
      "Value"
    )
  )
```

### Future costs per mile  

```{r future-cost-per-mile}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~`Mode/powertrain`, ~`Mode, fuel type`, ~`Cost per mile`,
  "Passenger", "PLDV-SI", "Light duty vehicle, gasoline", 0.62,
  "Passenger", "PLDV-CI", "Light duty vehicle, diesel", 0.62,
  "Passenger", "PLDV-HEV", "Light duty vehicle, hybrid", 0.55,
  "Passenger", "PLDV-PHEV", "Light duty vehicle, plug-in hybrid", 0.49,
  "Passenger", "PLDV-BEV", "Light duty vehicle, battery electric", 0.55,
  "Transit, bus", "Bus-BCI", "Bus, diesel", 2.91,
  "Transit, bus", "Bus-HEV", "Bus, hybrid", 2.82,
  "Transit, bus", "Bus-BEV", "Bus, battery electric", 2.73,
  "Transit, bus", "BRT-BCI", "Bus rapid transit, diesel", 4.01,
  "Transit, bus", "BRT-HEV", "Bus rapid transit, hybrid", 3.88,
  "Transit, bus", "BRT-BEV", "Bus rapid transit, battery electric", 3.76,
  "Transit, rail", "LRT-EV", "Light-rail, electric", 4.45,
  "Transit, rail", "RI-BCI", "Passenger rail, diesel", 4.43,
  "Transit, rail", "RI-EV", "Passenger rail, electric", 4.21,
  "School bus", "BS-CI", "Diesel", 2.43,
  "School bus", "BS-BEV", "Battery electric", 2.28,
  "Dynamic ride-sharing", "DRS-HEV", "Hybrid", 0.58,
  "Dynamic ride-sharing", "DRS-PHEV", "Plug-in hybrid", 0.52,
  "Dynamic ride-sharing", "DRS-BEV", "Battery electric", 0.59
) %>%
  dplyr::select(1, 3:4) %>%
  gt::gt(
    id = "future-cost-per-mile",
    caption = "Future transportation costs per mile",
    rowname_col = "Mode, fuel type",
    groupname_col = "group"
  ) %>%
  gt::opt_row_striping() %>%
  gt::fmt_currency(columns = 3) %>%
  gt::tab_footnote(
    "2020 dollars",
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels("Cost per mile")
  ) %>%
  gt::opt_row_striping() %>%
  gt::tab_options(row_group.font.weight = "bold")
```

**EXAMPLES**

Several cities are investing in large-scale tree planting programs as a means of decarbonization, including the Trillion Trees Initiative, the City of Los Angeles, the City of Tucson, and the City of Pittsburgh. In Minnesota, the City of Saint Paul 2011 Urban Canopy Assessment explored the potential for large-scale tree planting within the city.
